title: Loose Lips: Understanding Privacy Leakage in Agentic Dialogue
abstract: arXiv:2610.14071v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As LLM agents are increasingly deployed in high-stakes enterprise settings, understanding how they handle sensitive information in agentic dialogue has become critical. Privacy leakage in such settings requires reasoning about whether information flows respect the contextual norms under which they originated. We extend CIMemories to CIMEMORIES DIALOGUE, a benchmark of 4,410 two-agent dialogue instances grounded in Contextual Integrity theory. Using this benchmark, we systematically evaluate 7 open-weight models from the Qwen3 and Llama 3.1 families across conversation lengths of 1 and 6 turns under three prompting conditions. We find that task capability and privacy leakage are fundamentally coupled: more capable models are systematically leakier, with no model in our evaluation able to decouple the two. Thinking models consistently leak more than their non-thinking counterparts, a pattern we attribute to the extended reasoning surface

translated_title: 口风不严：理解智能体对话中的隐私泄露
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地被部署到高风险的企业环境中，理解它们在智能体对话中如何处理敏感信息已变得至关重要。此类环境下的隐私泄露问题需要推理判断信息流是否遵循其产生时所处情境的规范。我们将 CIMemories 扩展为 CIMEMORIES DIALOGUE，这是一个基于情境完整性理论的基准，包含 4,410 个双智能体对话实例。利用该基准，我们在三种提示条件下，对来自 Qwen3 和 Llama 3.1 家族的 7 个开放权重模型在 1 轮和 6 轮对话长度上进行了系统评估。我们发现，任务能力与隐私泄露在根本上是相互耦合的：能力越强的模型系统性地泄露更多隐私，而在我们的评估中没有任何模型能够将二者解耦。“思考型”模型始终比非思考型模型泄露更多隐私，我们将这一模式归因于其更长的推理过程。
tldr: 该研究提出基于情境完整性理论的CIMEMORIES DIALOGUE双智能体对话隐私基准，系统评估发现LLM智能体的任务能力与隐私泄露根本耦合——能力越强的模型泄露越严重，且思考型模型比非思考型模型泄露更多。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces CIMEMORIES DIALOGUE, a Contextual Integrity-based benchmark of two-agent dialogues, and reveals that LLM agents' task capability is fundamentally coupled with privacy leakage—more capable models are systematically leakier, and thinking models consistently leak more than non-thinking counterparts.
